base_setup_commands: apt-get update && apt-get install -y git curl wget make gcc g++ bash || true
setup_runtime_commands: conda create -n bioconda -y python conda-build conda-verify make wget gcc gxx
activation_validation_command: bash -c 'source /opt/conda/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate bioconda && echo ACTIVATION_OK'

runtime_profile.test_only_install_strategy: The test command 'alleleCounter -h' runs after building the recipe with conda-build. The built package installs alleleCounter binary which is then tested.
runtime_profile.notes: Bioconda environment for building conda recipes. Simplified to remove bioconda-utils (known import/conflict issues). Uses conda-build directly for building recipes. The cancerit-allelecount recipe builds a C-based tool that requires htslib, zlib, bzip2, and xz. Test is 'alleleCounter -h' which verifies the binary executes correctly.

notes: Base image is condaforge/mambaforge:latest with conda pre-installed at /opt/conda on Debian bookworm. Simplified package list removes bioconda-utils to avoid dependency conflicts (bioconda-utils requires conda-build 3.19.1.* which is not available). Uses channel_priority flexible to help conda resolve compatible versions. GCC/GXX are installed from conda-forge rather than gcc_linux-64/gxx_linux-64 to simplify. The test command 'alleleCounter -h' verifies the built binary works.
